epics.name: Reactivation V2 — for Sales users
epics.summary: Reactivation V2 helps Sales bring archived merchant locations back into the pipeline. It creates prefilled reactivation Leads for individual locations or in bulk, surfaces key churn and asset context, and manages inactive reactivation Opportunities automatically.

missions.name: 1. Reactivate one archived location → Lead
missions.goal: Confirm that Sales users can create a Reactivation Lead from an archived Account and that all relevant information already stored on the Account is copied to the new Lead.
missions.doneWhen: A Reactivation Lead is created with the expected prefilled fields; Lead Source = Reactivation; The Account remains archived.
steps: Log in to Staging as a Sales user (or Login As).
Open an archived (deleted) merchant Account in your country.
Click the Reactivation Lead button.
Confirm that a Lead is created with the expected prefilled fields and that Lead Source is Reactivation.
Return to the archived Account and click the Reactivation Lead button again. Confirm that an error message explains that a Reactivation Lead already exists.

missions.name: 2. Churn context visible on Lead (and Opp if available)
missions.goal: Verify that available churn context is displayed in a clear, read-only section on the Reactivation Lead and converted Opportunity, while the section remains hidden when no churn context exists.
missions.doneWhen: Churn Context section is visible when context exists; Hidden when empty; Read-only.
steps: Create a Reactivation Lead from an archived Account that has a Churn Opportunity.
Confirm the Churn Context section shows date, reason, sub-reason (if any), commentary.
Confirm you cannot edit it.
After converting the Lead, confirm that the Churn Context section also appears on the Opportunity and is read-only.
Create another Reactivation Lead from an archived Account without churn context. Confirm that the Churn Context section is hidden on the Lead.

missions.name: 3. Latest asset visible on Lead/Opp
missions.goal: Verify that the merchant's latest asset information is clearly displayed on the Reactivation Lead and remains available after the Lead is converted to an Opportunity.
missions.doneWhen: Latest asset info is visible on the reactivation Lead (and Opp if converted).
steps: Open a reactivation Lead for a merchant that has assets in Staging.
Confirm latest asset information is shown on the page.
Convert the Lead and confirm that the same latest asset information is displayed on the Opportunity.

missions.name: 4. Brand bulk reactivation
missions.goal: Verify that Sales users can bulk reactivate archived merchant locations from the Brand level.
missions.doneWhen: Rows for locations with an open Reactivation Lead are visible but cannot be selected; Selected eligible locations receive new Reactivation Leads.
steps: Open a Brand with several archived locations in Staging.
Select the location(s) you want to reactivate and click the Reactivation Lead button.
Confirm that new Reactivation Leads are created for the selected location(s).
Confirm that you cannot create a Lead for a location that already has an open Reactivation Lead.

missions.name: 5. Group bulk reactivation
missions.goal: Verify that Sales users can bulk reactivate archived merchant locations from the Group level.
missions.doneWhen: Rows for locations with an open Reactivation Lead are visible but cannot be selected; Selected eligible locations receive new Reactivation Leads; Brand column is visible.
steps: Open a Group with several archived locations in Staging.
Select the location(s) you want to reactivate and click the Reactivation Lead button.
Confirm that new Reactivation Leads are created for the selected location(s).
Confirm that you cannot create a Lead for a location that already has an open Reactivation Lead.

missions.name: 6. Reactivation Opp
missions.goal: Verify that the workflow for a Reactivation Opportunity is the same as the workflow for a new Sales Opportunity.
missions.doneWhen: The user cannot create a duplicate Reactivation Opportunity; The user can mark the Opportunity as Won; Features available on a Sales Opportunity work correctly on a Reactivation Opportunity.
steps: Convert a Reactivation Lead to create a Reactivation Opportunity, or open an existing Reactivation Opportunity.
Confirm that the Parent Opportunity and Child Opportunity structure is the same as for a standard new onboarding Opportunity.
Confirm that the Opportunity Type is Reactivation.
Confirm that the user can mark the Opportunity as Won by following the standard new onboarding Opportunity workflow.
Confirm that a Case is created after the Opportunity is marked as Won.
After the Opportunity is marked as Won, open the Account's Reactivation tab. Confirm that the status is Onboarding and that the other activation-related fields have been cleared.
